The original purpose of MarijuanaNews was simply to report the crimes being committed under marijuana prohibition, and to document the failure of “journalism” to report it. Primarily because of the Initiative process, the American people were able to force changes in the laws, and our leaders and our fearless media are almost catching up with events.

For example, around nine-in-ten U.S. adults say that marijuana should be legal for medical use, and the Congress and the Administration are seriously considering removing it from Schedule 1, which says that it has no medical use.

See

Oh, The Irony! As Prohibitionists Have Fits Over Rescheduling Cannabis, Over-the-Counter Pain Relievers Found to Be More Dangerous Than Thought

 

Of course our fearless media can’t quite get the story right, but they have only had a quarter of a century.

 

From 1999, See IOM Acknowledges:

"There is no clear alternative for people suffering from chronic conditions that might be relieved by smoking marijuana, such as pain or AIDS wasting." But Still Opposes Smoked Marijuana -- NORML Special Bulletin

 

“Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it"  George Santayana

 

If we forget about the sacrifices, the suffering, and even the deaths of those who fought to get us this far, then we don’t deserve to be free, but they deserve better of us.

See Lest We Forget: From Twenty Years Ago, July 12,2005:The Murder of Steve McWilliams. An Indictment, Not An Obituary. The Absurdity of Evil. Condolences from NORML.

 

Posted September 23, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan

 

"Government is not reason, it is not eloquence - it is force! Like fire it is a dangerous servant and a fearful master: never for a moment should it be left to irresponsible action. " George Washington

That this warning by George Washington should be relevant today is truly the great American tragedy. A recent report from California attorney William McPike, a member of the NORML legal committee, has caused me to try once again to understand the nature of our sickness.

 

McPike relates that in Fresno County, two patients, a husband and wife, both whom have doctor's recommendations were growing six plants in their backyard. Some kids jumped over their fence to try to steal some of their medicine. Inasmuch as the couple are legal under Prop 215, and six plants is even the minimum number allowed under a new law (yet to be signed by Governor Davis) they felt quite comfortable calling the Clovis, California, police.

The police who came to their house were very helpful and even gave the couple some ideas on securing the plants and left the patients happy. However, two days later, narks arrived with NO warrant, but instead served a single page Notice of Service of Warrant, which McPike says is usually all they serve in Fresno County.

 

The Notice simply states: " If you want further info you may contact [the narcs]. They also took the six plants and a legal shotgun, pellet gun, and even their medical recommendations. The patients had to post bail.

 

But, wait, it gets worse

The narcs issued a press release giving the couple's exact address and their names. In the press release, they say, “ While medical marijuana may be legal in California, Fresno County has a no tolerance policy toward cultivation of marijuana. "

 

They actually had the press release before the warrant, assuming they have a warrant. In other words, the police are so brazen that they will issue a press release announcing that they are violating the state law and Constitution!

 

The Encyclopædia Britannica says sociopaths are marked by a personal history of chronic and continuous antisocial behavior, in which the rights of others are violated, and by poor or nonexistent job performance

 

This is also a perfect description of the actions of these narcs and the narcocracy in general.

 

How is it possible that the American people not only tolerate this sort of behavior, but often even approve of it. There are many historical examples of people being frightened into giving up their freedom in exchange for protection from both real and imaginary threats. Foreign enemies and racial minorities at home have been used as bogeymen to justify increases in state power.

 

No one would think of author William S. Burroughs (Naked Lunch) as a sober political analyst, but in 1947 he presciently warned,

"I believe in the near future, the government will use anti-drug hysteria to set up a police state "

 

I have repeatedly described the role that marijuana prohibition plays in this process.
See
Learning About Prohibitionism: House Debate on Medical Marijuana Bill Offers New Insight Into Police State Ideology.
and
All Power to The Incompetents: UK Cannabis Reform Delayed As Police Push for Arbitrary Power. Fail to Protect Royal Family, But Demand Control Over Cannabis. More That We Couldn't Make Up.
and
The Police Fraud. Someone Is Lying. Marking The 30th Anniversary Of An Article in National Review. What if Don Quixote Was Right? Analysis by Richard Cowan

However, I have not yet succeeded in describing how profoundly pathological this is. If it is a fundamental threat to a country like the United States and the United Kingdom, it is an even greater threat to countries with less developed institutions and traditions of liberty.
See
Is The UN An Instrument of Peace and Freedom Or Of War and Tyranny? UN Narks Make Answer Clear. Lies and Hatred In Service To International Police State. (International Narcotics Control Board Report)

It is also especially disturbing and puzzling that minority communities that suffer the most from prohibition are often its strongest supporters. This reminded me of what is called the Stockholm Syndrome which has nothing to do with the wacky Swedish prohibitionists.

 

In 1973, four people in Stockholm were held hostage in a bank vault for six days during a robbery and became psychologically attached to their captors. This seemingly paradoxical phenomenon was then dubbed the Stockholm Syndrome.

In Psychological Responses to TerrorismRev. Fr. Charles T. Brusca, explains, Long-term psychological study of this and similar hostage situations has defined a fairly clear and characteristic set of symptoms for the Stockholm Syndrome

:

The captives begin to identify with their captors. At least at first this is a defensive mechanism, based on the (often unconscious) idea that the captor will not hurt the captive if he is cooperative and even positively supportive. The captive seeks to win the favor of the captor in an almost childlike way...

 

Long term captivity builds even stronger attachment to the captor as he becomes known as a human being with his own problems and aspirations. Particularly in political or ideological situations, longer captivity also allows the captive to become familiar with the captor's point of view and the history of his grievances against authority. He may come to believe that the captor's position is just.

This strange behavior can be partly explained by the fact that the hostages are necessarily isolated from other sources of information so that their captors control their world view. The collaboration between the media and the narcocracy in supporting cannabis prohibition is the societal equivalent of this phenomenon.

 

Orwell wrote that " Political language...is designed to make lies sound truthful and murder respectable, and to give an appearance of solidity to pure wind. That is a perfect description of cannabis prohibition.

On the other hand, we have it on the highest authority that the truth will make us free, but it is important to understand that freed hostages actually remain unfree until they overcome the hostage mentality that is called the Stockholm Syndrome.

 

In fact, our chains are really in our minds and that is why only open allegiance to the truth will make us free. We must call lies lies before we can call ourselves truly free.
From 2002
